cast/string/from-int-past-exponent-thres.reason: Prisma filters have no cast operator: string() over int() has no column to solve for, and CEL renders the int as "1000000" where the double it came from would be "1e+06", so it cannot be solved as a string() over the number column.

comparison/equals/whole-list-literal.reason: Prisma scalar comparison and membership inputs cannot bind list or map elements; the translator refuses before constructing a filter.

comparison/equals/whole-list-literal-ord.reason: Prisma scalar comparison and membership inputs cannot bind list or map elements, and an ordered, multiplicity-counting list equality (with a null element) has no relation filter form; the translator refuses before constructing a filter.

comparison/not-equals/whole-list-literal.reason: Prisma scalar comparison and membership inputs cannot bind list or map elements; the translator refuses before constructing a filter.

hierarchy/descendent-of/bracket-in-path.reason: Hierarchy prefixes containing [ cannot be matched literally: Prisma emits LIKE without an ESCAPE clause, and [ opens a character class on SQL Server even when one is declared

hierarchy/descendent-of/like-metacharact.reason: Hierarchy descendant prefixes require literal LIKE matching, but Prisma string filters cannot escape % or _; the adapter throws instead of treating them as wildcards

string/concatenate/ordering.reason: Both operands of the concatenation are columns: aString + aOptionalString has no value side to solve against, and Prisma filters cannot concatenate columns or compare a computed string

string/contains/field-to-field.reason: A column-valued needle would need per-row LIKE escaping, which Prisma filters cannot express; the adapter throws

string/ends-with/backslash-in-needle.reason: A backslash is a LIKE metacharacter on some providers and not others, so the same needle cannot mean the same thing on all of them: SQLite's LIKE has no escape character and matches a backslash literally, while PostgreSQL and MySQL treat it as the DEFAULT escape character with no ESCAPE clause present. endsWith('\\') is then a pattern ending in an escape character, which PostgreSQL rejects outright (SQLSTATE 22025), and a backslash anywhere inside a needle silently escapes the next character so contains('a\\b') would match 'ab' — a row the PDP denies. string/ends-with/field-to-field.reason: Same column-needle LIKE limitation as string/contains/field-to-field

string/starts-with/percent-in-needle.reason: Prisma emits LIKE without an ESCAPE clause and does not escape wildcards, so a needle containing % or _ cannot be matched literally; the adapter throws instead of filtering wrong
